stem: Why is cycloplegia useful in chemical conjunctivitis?

options.text: Some chemicals cause ciliary spasm, which contributes to pain
It neutralises alkali on the ocular surface
It removes lime particles from the conjunctiva
It confirms whether pseudostrabismus is present
It reverses corneal penetration by alkali

explanation: Cycloplegia is useful because some chemicals cause ciliary spasm, which contributes to pain.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Chemical Conjunctivitis

optionExplanations.A: Correct because some chemicals cause ciliary spasm, and cycloplegia reduces the associated pain.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because cycloplegia does not neutralise alkali on the ocular surface; irrigation is used for that purpose.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because removing lime particles requires physical removal and irrigation, not cycloplegia.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because cycloplegia is unrelated to assessing pseudostrabismus.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because cycloplegia does not reverse alkali penetration of the cornea.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
